scope: Trusted logical document publication, immutable manifests, guarded native retrieval, current-version revalidation and durable cross-process provenance

verification.skipReason: Optional real-provider test is not enabled

architecture.publication: JdbcLabelStore delegates to a separate JdbcDocumentCatalog; root document head and full immutable manifest committed together using row lock and expected-version CAS
architecture.identity: Full host-bound DataResource + documentId + monotonic version + segmentId + actual content digest; AGT-FRAGMENT-V2, original unversioned V1 keys preserved
architecture.trustedBinding: Explicit host DocumentResolver rather than trusting source metadata; actual TextSegment text is hashed and compared with published manifest
architecture.classification: Document-level grade cannot decrease across replacement or withdrawal; versioned provenance retains content-level grade; duplicate text across documents joins conservative labels without idempotency collision
architecture.causality: Versioned classification references manifest and content-level history; derived content events retain original data-action reference
architecture.boundaries: Current published version checked before retrieval delivery, later action authorization/dispatch, and remote model/tool response checks; shutdown cleanup is not blocked by stale context
architecture.recovery: Version reference serialized in existing fragment checkpoint and action-bound metadata protocol; fresh JDBC authority retains identity and rejects stale context during subsequent operations
architecture.privacy: Manifest/work protocol contains IDs, digests, classifications and provenance; no document/query/model response body added

cases: Durable history, idempotent retry after a later publication, monotonic classification and empty-manifest withdrawal
Eight independent concurrent fresh publishers: exactly one expected-version success
Wrong expected version and reused action with changed content rejected without head mutation
Missing schema and damaged manifest fail closed
Maximum manifest round-trip; overflow and inconsistent caller container size rejected without truncation
Caller mutates input while database connection is gated: immutable prepared manifest and original idempotent fingerprint retained
Synchronous/asynchronous original content classification overrides forged source metadata and prevents low-clearance native model dispatch
Old published version rejected; falsely claiming current version with old text rejected
Native asynchronous retrieval held while new version publishes: no result delivered
Publish during model preparation: native model counter remains zero, unused external work safely NOT_STARTED
Content grade before/after retrieval cannot be washed by adding version reference
Two same-text results from public/secret documents in one retrieval: valid batch joins SECRET and model dispatch remains zero
Actual delegated receiver model starts, publishes replacement during native execution, then POST_MODEL_CALL rejects its result as document_version_stale
Explicit versioned wrapper requires flow and catalog; no silent fallback

wireTests.DocumentFragmentTest: Two tests cover V1 stability, V2 distinction, JSON numeric round-trip, immutable expected references and invalid shape/type rejection
wireTests.FlowProjectionTest: Strict canonical JSON comparison accepts parsed integer representation without accepting extra body fields

independentProcess.topology: Two independent SDK JVMs per variant, authenticated loopback HTTP status service and file-backed H2 JDBC authority
assertions: Public document reaches native model once
Sensitive document remains CONFIDENTIAL even when version manifest and forged metadata claim PUBLIC; native model dispatch zero
Fresh JDBC registry retains fragment identity, grade and original data-action association
Publishing next version after restore causes parent output to reject stale context
Captured authorization RPC contains no synthetic document/query/model body
independentProcess.fixtureTiming: Overall child await allows ten seconds and parent read twenty seconds for multiple bounded RPC/file commits; production one-second RPC and lease constraints unchanged

candidates.name: LangChain RecordManager
candidates.fit: Index hash/source tracking and synchronization; Python deployment does not replace Java authorization/dispatch integration

candidates.name: Qdrant conditional updates
candidates.fit: Can support host indexing/version conditions; requires vector service or migration and does not provide this SDK trust binding

spike.decision: Reuse existing JDBC runtime/catalog and native ContentRetriever integration; no new external service dependency
spike.validation: Official interfaces/license reviewed; candidate services were not deployed

limitations: Trusted ingestion, backend binding and database access control are required; manifest is not injection detection or proof of content authenticity
Only current published versions allowed; stale tasks must start fresh, contexts are not silently rewritten
No vector-store/manifest distributed transaction, embedding generation or old-vector deletion
A check observes catalog state at its boundary, not a lock across remote generation; already delivered bytes and side effects cannot be rolled back
Unversioned wrappers preserve original semantics and cannot claim logical-version protection
No tamper-proof audit or database-admin/backup-rollback attestation
Only H2 and local authenticated HTTP fixtures validated; production database migration, IAM and HA remain open
Production provider termination, platform checks and P1 injection, side effects, audit, approval and supply-chain work remain active
